### Is there an already existing issue for this? - [x] I have searched the existing issues ### Expected behavior With the SHM transport, a DataReader in another process on the same host wakes as soon as a sample is written. On macOS that should take tens of microseconds, the same as with UDPv4 on the same Mac (50–110 µs, below). ### Current behavior On macOS, a DataReader in another process only notices new SHM data on a fixed tick of about 5.7 ms, whatever the publish rate. As a result: - **Latency:** median ~2.9 ms, p99 ~5.7 ms, from 50 Hz to 5 kHz. - **Bursts:** at 2 kHz, samples arrive in groups of ~11 every ~5.7 ms. - **Loss with KEEP_LAST 1:** all but the newest sample of each burst are replaced before the reader runs: 2000 Hz published, 354–450 Hz received. - **Idle CPU:** an idle reader process uses ~5 % of a core polling. Cyclone DDS on the same machine uses ~0. - **Collapse under overload:** from 100 kHz upward (`Float64`, reader KEEP_LAST 100), the reader receives **0.0–1.5 %** of samples with 0.1–2.9 s latency. That held in every run, including SHM-only (`FASTDDS_BUILTIN_TRANSPORTS=SHM`). Over UDPv4 alone the same rates deliver 37–51 %. With SHM removed (`FASTDDS_BUILTIN_TRANSPORTS=UDPv4`), the same test gives 78–87 µs median and no loss. ### Root cause **The stack.** `sample` on the reader process shows the SHM listener thread (`dds.shm.`) here for ~95 % of samples: ``` eprosima::fastdds::rtps::SharedMemGlobal::Port::wait_pop RobustInterprocessCondition::timed_wait / do_timed_wait boost::interprocess::ipcdetail::try_based_timed_lock> boost::interprocess::spin_wait::yield() nanosleep ``` **How the bundled Boost (master) gets there:** 1. `thirdparty/boost/include/boost/interprocess/detail/workaround.hpp` - On `__APPLE__` it defines `BOOST_INTERPROCESS_BUGGY_POSIX_PROCESS_SHARED`, because Darwin's `pthread_cond` stores a mutex pointer inside the condition, so `BOOST_INTERPROCESS_POSIX_PROCESS_SHARED` is not set. - It also leaves `BOOST_INTERPROCESS_POSIX_UNNAMED_SEMAPHORES` unset ("MacOsX declares _POSIX_SEMAPHORES but sem_init returns ENOSYS"). 2. `sync/interprocess_semaphore.hpp` uses POSIX semaphores only when both macros are set. Otherwise it falls back to `spin/semaphore.hpp`, and `interprocess_mutex` likewise falls back to `spin_mutex`. 3. `RobustInterprocessCondition` blocks each waiter on a `bi::interprocess_semaphore` (`SemaphoreNode::sem`). On macOS that is the spin semaphore: `try_based_timed_lock` → `spin_wait::yield()`. 4. Once the yield-only budget of one system tick is used up, `spin_wait` alternates `thread_yield()` and `thread_sleep_tick()`. On POSIX, `thread_sleep_tick()` is `nanosleep(get_system_tick_ns() / 2)` (`detail/os_thread_functions.hpp`). 5. On macOS, `sysconf(_SC_CLK_TCK)` is 100. That gives a 10 ms tick and a 5 ms sleep request, and `nanosleep(5 ms)` measured 6.04–6.11 ms mean / 7.1–9.3 ms max on this machine. That sleep is the observed ~5.7 ms tick, and its average half-period is the ~2.9 ms median latency. **Causation check.** I injected a `nanosleep` interposer (`DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`) that shortens only the 5 ms request. That alone moves latency and loss, with no other change to Fast DDS: | Sleep per poll | Received of 2000 Hz (KEEP_LAST 1) | Latency p50 / p99 | Idle reader CPU | |---|---|---|---| | 5 ms (stock) | 377 Hz | 0.93 / 5.56 ms | 5.6 % | | 1 ms | 919 Hz | 0.28 / 1.09 ms | 6.3 % | | 200 µs | 1992 Hz | 0.13 / 0.31 ms | 10.2 % | | 50 µs | 1864 Hz | 0.06 / 1.16 ms | 19.0 % | Shorter sleeps only trade latency for CPU, so a real blocking primitive is needed (see possible fixes below). ### Steps to reproduce Two processes on one Mac with default transports, ROS 2 `rclcpp`, `std_msgs/msg/Float64`, `BEST_EFFORT`. Data-sharing is not involved: there are no `DataSharing` frames in the profile.
repro.cpp (run repro sub 1 and repro pub 1; the argument is the KEEP_LAST depth) ```cpp #include #include #include #include #include #include #include #include using namespace std::chrono; static double now_us() {return duration(steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count();} int main(int argc, char ** argv) { rclcpp::init(argc, argv); const bool pub = argc > 1 && !strcmp(argv[1], "pub"); const int depth = argc > 2 ? atoi(argv[2]) : 1; auto node = std::make_shared(pub ? "repro_pub" : "repro_sub"); auto qos = rclcpp::QoS(depth).best_effort(); rclcpp::Publisher::SharedPtr p; rclcpp::Subscription::SharedPtr s; rclcpp::TimerBase::SharedPtr t; std::vector lat; if (pub) { // 2 kHz, payload = send time p = node->create_publisher("repro", qos); t = node->create_wall_timer(500us, [&] {std_msgs::msg::Float64 m; m.data = now_us(); p->publish(m);}); } else { // print rate and latency every 2 s s = node->create_subscription("repro", qos, [&](std_msgs::msg::Float64::ConstSharedPtr m) { lat.push_back(now_us() - m->data);}); t = node->create_wall_timer(2s, [&] { if (lat.empty()) {return;} std::sort(lat.begin(), lat.end()); printf("received %.0f Hz latency p50 %.0f us p99 %.0f us\n", lat.size() / 2.0, lat[lat.size() / 2], lat[lat.size() * 99 / 100]); fflush(stdout); lat.clear();}); } rclcpp::spin(node); rclcpp::shutdown(); } ```
Full benchmark, scripts and the root-cause tools (`nanosleep` shim, `os_sync_wait_on_address` demo): https://github.com/idesign0/ros2-macos-rmw-bench All numbers below are from Release (`-O3`) builds, on a quiet machine, with ranges over repeated runs. **Reproducer output.** ROS 2 Kilted (Fast DDS 3.2.5), 2 kHz publisher: | RMW / transport | KEEP_LAST | Received | Latency p50 / p99 | / 5.74 ms (bursts) | | 2.14.7 (Jazzy) | SHM only, KEEP_LAST 100 | 8000 / 8000 | 2.86 / 5.68 ms | 2 µs / 5.75 ms (bursts) | | 2.14.7 (Jazzy) | UDPv4 only | 1999 Hz | 78 / 284 µs | 500 / 651 µs | | 3.2.5 (Kilted) | default | 428 Hz | 1.50 / 5.53 ms | 0.07 / 5.80 ms | | 3.2.5 (Kilted) | default, KEEP_LAST 100 | 7980–7999 / 8000 | 2.86–2.89 / 5.64–6.27 ms | 2 µs / 5.74 ms (bursts) | | 3.2.5 (Kilted) | SHM only, KEEP_LAST 100 | 7998 / 8000 | 2.85 / 5.63 ms | 2 µs / 5.73 ms (bursts) | | 3.2.5 (Kilted) | UDPv4 only | 2000 Hz | 79 / 122 µs | 500 / 560 µs | **Sustained rate between two processes** (Fast DDS 3.2.5, `Float64`, KEEP_LAST 100, `sleep_until`-paced publisher): | Publish rate | Default (SHM + UDPv4): received, p50 / p99 | UDPv4 only: received, p50 / p99 | |---|---|---| | 5 kHz | 100 %, 2.9 / 5.7 ms | 100 %, 55 / 116 µs | | 20 kHz | 99.9 %, 3.1 / 5.7 ms | 100 %, 48 / 103 µs | | 50 kHz | 96.0 %, 3.5 / 5.8 ms | 100 %, 82 µs / 20 ms | | 100 kHz | **1.5 %**, 0.25 / 0.61 s | 51 %, 80 / 82 ms | | flat out (~117–128 kHz) | **0.0 %**, 1.6 / 2.9 s | 41 %, 79 / 81 ms | For reference on the same Mac: - Cyclone DDS (UDP): 100 % at 50 kHz (22 / 52 µs). - Cyclone DDS + iceoryx: 100 % at 200 kHz (10 / 27 µs). - Zenoh with batching off: 100 % up to its ~90 kHz publisher limit (53 / 97 µs). **The tick does not depend on rate.** Fast DDS 3.2.5, default transports, `Float64`, KEEP_LAST 100: | Publish rate | Latency p50 / p99 | |---|---| | 50 Hz | 3.28 / 5.90 ms | | 200 Hz | 2.83 / 5.66 ms | | 2000 Hz | 2.86 / 5.64 ms | | 5000 Hz | 2.92 / 5.69 ms | ### Fast DDS version/commit - **Measured:** 2.14.7 (ROS 2 Jazzy) and 3.2.5 (ROS 2 Kilted). - **Code paths on `master`:** `RobustInterprocessCondition.hpp`, the bundled Boost `workaround.hpp`, `interprocess_semaphore.hpp` and `os_thread_functions.hpp` are as described above. ### Platform/Architecture Other. Please specify in Additional context section. ### Transport layer Shared Memory Transport (SHM) ### Additional context **Platform:** macOS 27.0.1 (Darwin 27.0.0), Apple Silicon arm64 (MacBook Pro M2, Mac14,7), Apple clang. ROS 2 built from source via the Homebrew tap `idesign0/homebrew-ros2`. **Possible fixes** (from least to most invasive): 1. **Futex-style semaphore on Apple (suggested).** macOS 14.4+ has public, cross-process wait/wake on a word in shared memory: ``, functions `os_sync_wait_on_address`, `os_sync_wait_on_address_with_timeout` and `os_sync_wake_by_address_any/all`, used with `OS_SYNC_WAIT_ON_ADDRESS_SHARED` / `OS_SYNC_WAKE_BY_ADDRESS_SHARED`. - **What it replaces:** only `SemaphoreNode::sem` in `RobustInterprocessCondition` (one counter per waiter, already in shared memory). - **Shape of the change:** - wait: a CAS-decrement loop, blocking with `os_sync_wait_on_address_with_timeout(&count, 0, 4, SHARED, OS_CLOCK_MACH_ABSOLUTE_TIME, ns)` while the count is 0; - post: `fetch_add` followed by `os_sync_wake_by_address_any(&count, 4, SHARED)`; - older macOS: guard with `__builtin_available(macOS 14.4, *)` and keep the current fallback. - **Measured here:** a standalone two-process test (shared memory via `shm_open`/`mmap`, 2 kHz) woke the waiter in **5.9–9.7 µs p50 / 16–26 µs p99** over three runs. The waiter used **1–1.5 % CPU**, and nothing while idle. 2. **Named POSIX semaphores** (`sem_open`, which works on macOS) per waiter slot. They block in the kernel and work on older macOS, but the names need cleanup when a process crashes, which `RobustInterprocessCondition` would have to handle. 3. **A kernel "doorbell" per port**, such as a FIFO or `AF_UNIX` datagram socket: the writer sends a byte after pushing to the ring buffer, and the reader blocks in `read`/`kevent`. Portable and robust, but one extra syscall per notification. 4. **Stop-gap only:** have `thread_sleep_tick()` sleep much less than `tick/2` on Apple (Fast DDS already patches its bundled Boost via `BOOST_FASTDDS_PATCHES`). The table above shows the CPU cost, so this only reduces the latency. Separately, possibly unrelated to SHM: with `RMW_FASTRTPS_PUBLICATION_MODE=ASYNCHRONOUS` and UDPv4 only, `publish()` failed with `cannot publish data` (`rmw_publish.cpp:68`) and aborted the publisher at 5 kHz (`Float64`, KEEP_LAST 1). Happy to open a separate issue if useful. `interprocess_mutex` is also `spin_mutex` on Apple, so contended SHM mutexes can hit the same 5 ms sleep. That's not measured separately here. **Workarounds for users today:** - **Disable SHM:** `FASTDDS_BUILTIN_TRANSPORTS=UDPv4`, or an XML profile with only UDPv4. - **ROS 2 caveat:** under `ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=LOCALHOST`, `rmw_fastrtps` sets `use_builtin_transports = false` and adds SHM itself (`rmw_fastrtps_shared_cpp/src/participant.cpp`, Jazzy and Kilted). The variable is then ignored, and I measured the same 316–332 Hz / 5 ms behaviour in that mode. - **Deeper KEEP_LAST queue:** avoids the loss but not the latency. - **One process (ROS 2 composition):** load publisher and subscriber as components into the same `component_container` with `use_intra_process_comms: true`, so samples don't cross processes and SHM is not used. Fast DDS 2.14.7, 2 kHz, 64 B: 1989 Hz received, latency 14 / 40 µs p50 / p99. In one process without intra-process comms, Fast DDS delivery also avoids the tick: 2000 Hz, 25 / 48 µs. This only helps for nodes that can share a process. ### XML configuration file No XML. Default transports (ROS 2 `rmw_fastrtps_cpp` defaults), `ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=SUBNET`. ### Relevant log output _No response_ ### Network traffic capture _No response_

new_candidates.body:
## Problem

CameraSensor publishes gz::msgs::Image before invoking
ConnectImageCallback. An external integration that needs to attach
simulation-time pose or hardware timestamp metadata must therefore
subscribe to the already-published image and republish the complete
pixel payload.

This creates two large image deliveries per frame.

## Use case

A camera-pose synchronization plugin associates every rendered image
with the camera's world pose at the image simulation timestamp.

## Measured result

320×240 RGB at 10 FPS:

- Current republish design: 4.6249 MB/s
- External raw-image + pose design: 4.6180 MB/s
- Integrated single-publication estimate: 2.313 MB/s

Both external designs still involve two large publisher-subscriber
delivery pairs.

## Proposed direction

Provide a pre-publication callback or transformation API:

using ImageMutator =
    std::function<void(gz::msgs::Image &)>;

ConnectionPtr ConnectImageMutator(ImageMutator callback);

CameraSensor::Update():
    populate image;
    invoke image mutators;
    publisher.Publish(image);
    invoke ordinary const observers;

The exact API is open for maintainer discussion.
new_candidates.title: Feature request: pre-publication camera image callback for synchronized pose metadata

new_candidates.body:
## Environment
* OS Version: Ubuntu 24.04
* Source build of `main`, measured at 10ce31be9. The code linked below is the same at 33871d08b and in `gz-sim8`, `gz-sim9` and `gz-sim10`.
* Rendering plugin: ogre2, NVIDIA RTX 4060 Ti. The problem is in how often frames are drawn, not in the rendering itself.

## Description

A DVL sensor makes the Sensors system draw a frame on every simulation iteration, whatever the DVL's update rate. The simulation waits for each of those frames. In `examples/worlds/dvl_world.sdf` the DVL runs at 1 Hz with 1 ms steps, so it costs 1000 frames per simulated second instead of 1.

Why:
* The DVL is a custom sensor (`type="custom" gz:type="dvl"`). The Sensors system does not create it, so it does not know its update rate. The DVL system creates the `gz::sensors::DopplerVelocityLog` itself, in the rendering thread, and updates it from the `PreRender`, `Render` and `PostRender` events: [DopplerVelocityLogSystem.cc#L237-L248](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/33871d08ba035539d09492136a18b0ea0baeb01c/src/systems/dvl/DopplerVelocityLogSystem.cc#L237-L248)
* The Sensors system renders on every iteration while anything is connected to those three events, because it cannot know when the callbacks need a frame. The `\todo` there already points at the cost: [Sensors.cc#L993-L1001](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/33871d08ba035539d09492136a18b0ea0baeb01c/src/systems/sensors/Sensors.cc#L993-L1001)
* The DVL does not need those frames. It already asks for the frames it needs with `ForceRender` when it has new data: [DopplerVelocityLogSystem.cc#L405-L407](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/33871d08ba035539d09492136a18b0ea0baeb01c/src/systems/dvl/DopplerVelocityLogSystem.cc#L405-L407)

The built-in rendering sensors (camera, depth camera, GPU lidar, thermal, segmentation, ...) are not affected: the Sensors system creates them and draws a frame only when one of them is due. The other sensors (IMU, CPU lidar, altimeter, ...) do not use the rendering thread. Any out-of-tree rendering sensor written like the DVL, which is what the `ForceRender` documentation suggests, has the same problem.

There is a second bug behind this one: `ForceRender` alone never draws a frame. `ForceRender()` sets `forceUpdate`, but `PostUpdate` overwrites it with `PendingSensors() > 0 || hasRenderConnections` before the rendering thread reads it ([Sensors.cc#L1051-L1056](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/33871d08ba035539d09492136a18b0ea0baeb01c/src/systems/sensors/Sensors.cc#L1051-L1056)). Nobody noticed because the DVL's connections draw a frame on every iteration anyway. Without those frames the DVL would get none.

* Expected behavior: the DVL costs frames at its own update rate, like a camera does.
* Actual behavior: a frame on every iteration while the DVL system is loaded, even with no DVL sensor in the world.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Copy `examples/worlds/dvl_world.sdf` and set `<real_time_factor>0</real_time_factor>` so that it runs as fast as it can.
2. Run it with a subscriber on `/dvl/velocity`: `gz sim -s -r --headless-rendering --iterations 100000 dvl_world.sdf`, and read the real time factor from `gz topic -e -t /world/dvl_world/stats`.
3. Remove the `gz-sim-dvl-system` plugin from the copy and run it again.

## Output

`dvl_world.sdf` with `real_time_factor` 0, 100000 iterations of 1 ms, two runs each. RTF from `/world/dvl_world/stats`, without the first 20% of the run (startup):

| | Frames drawn | RTF |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | one per iteration | 19.6, 20.0 |
| `main` without `gz-sim-dvl-system` | none | 29.2, 30.7 |
| `main` with the change proposed below | one per DVL update | 21.0, 22.1 |

The frames were counted with a local frame counter, at `real_time_factor` 1: 4962 frames for 4962 iterations on `main`, 5 frames for 4959 iterations with the change.

In this world a forced frame is cheap (there is little to update) and mostly overlaps with the physics step, so the forced frames cost about 10% of the RTF. Most of the rest is the DVL's own update: with nothing subscribed to `/dvl/velocity` the RTF is 23.4 and 23.6 on `main`, 26.3 and 26.4 with the change.

The forced frames cost much more when the scene is larger. A vehicle with a 10 Hz camera and a 1 Hz DVL over 144 rock models, 1 ms steps: on `main` the forced frames took 72% of the rendering thread time and the RTF was 8.6 to 8.9. With the DVL drawing frames only when it is due, the RTF was 42.2 to 42.8 (x4.8). The DVL and camera output was byte-identical with `--seed 1`, in that world and in `dvl_world.sdf`.

## Proposal

* A new event, `events::OnDemandRenderConnections`, with which a system says that its connections to `PreRender`, `Render` and `PostRender` only need the frames that it asks for with `ForceRender`. The Sensors system keeps drawing a frame on every iteration if any connection is not counted, so other systems and third-party plugins keep today's behaviour.
* Fix `ForceRender` so that it draws a frame on its own.
* The DVL system counts its connections, asks for frames when a sensor is due, and uses the world state of the frame's own iteration.

The event and the `ForceRender` fix are on [`jrivero/render_on_demand`](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/tree/jrivero/render_on_demand). I'll open a pull request with the DVL changes.

Assisted-By: Claude Opus 5.5
new_candidates.title: DVL system makes the Sensors system draw a frame on every iteration

new_candidates.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a hardware component's `read()` (or `write()`) returns `ERROR` once, its `on_error()` is called
**twice** if `on_error()` returns `FAILURE` or `ERROR`. The second call happens on a component that is
already `finalized`. If `on_error()` returns `SUCCESS`, it is called once, as expected.

Cause, as far as I can tell from the source (links are to `master` @ 97e42ad with the same code on `jazzy` 4.48.1):

1. `HardwareComponent::read()` calls `error()` itself when `trigger_read()` returns `ERROR`
   ([hardware_component.cpp#L316](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/blob/97e42adf87e9eb9c870bb2d4c00985daca86b8bd/hardware_interface/src/hardware_component.cpp#L316)), and returns `ERROR`.
2. `ResourceManager::read()` sees `ret_val != OK` and calls `component.error()` again
   ([resource_manager.cpp#L2496](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/blob/97e42adf87e9eb9c870bb2d4c00985daca86b8bd/hardware_interface/src/resource_manager.cpp#L2496)).
3. `HardwareComponent::error()` only skips `on_error()` when the component is `UNKNOWN` or
   `UNCONFIGURED` ([hardware_component.cpp#L226-L228](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/blob/97e42adf87e9eb9c870bb2d4c00985daca86b8bd/hardware_interface/src/hardware_component.cpp#L226-L228)).
   - `on_error()` → `SUCCESS`: component becomes `UNCONFIGURED`, so the second `error()` is a no-op.
   - `on_error()` → `FAILURE`/`ERROR`: component becomes `FINALIZED`
     ([L239-L243](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/blob/97e42adf87e9eb9c870bb2d4c00985daca86b8bd/hardware_interface/src/hardware_component.cpp#L239-L243)), which is not covered by the check, so
     `on_error()` runs a second time.

The write path has the same pair ([hardware_component.cpp#L355](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/blob/97e42adf87e9eb9c870bb2d4c00985daca86b8bd/hardware_interface/src/hardware_component.cpp#L355),
[resource_manager.cpp#L2595](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/blob/97e42adf87e9eb9c870bb2d4c00985daca86b8bd/hardware_interface/src/resource_manager.cpp#L2595)); I only reproduced the read path.

The second `error()` call came with #1730. In its review a guard was suggested "to avoid calling
on_error() twice", and the `UNCONFIGURED` check was added, but it does not cover the `FINALIZED` case.

Why it matters: `FAILURE` from `on_error()` means "I could not bring the hardware to a safe state".
A driver then gets `on_error()` again after it has already given up and possibly released its
resources (closed the bus, freed handles). On my real robot (Feetech so101 servo arm), the first call failed
to switch torque off, closed the serial port and returned `FAILURE`; the second call 2 ms later ran
against the closed port and only stayed harmless because of an explicit `is_open()` check.

**To Reproduce**

Minimal package, no hardware: one joint, `read()` returns `ERROR` exactly once (10th call),
`on_error()` counts its calls and returns what the `on_error_result` hardware parameter says.
Only `robot_state_publisher` and `ros2_control_node` are started; no controllers.

1. Create the package below in a workspace and `colcon build`.
2. `ros2 launch on_error_repro repro.launch.py on_error_result:=failure`
3. `ros2 launch on_error_repro repro.launch.py on_error_result:=success`

Output, case 2 (`failure`):
```
[WARN]  [controller_manager.hardware_component.system.ErrorTwice]: read() #10 returns ERROR (the only failure)
[ERROR] [controller_manager.hardware_component.system.ErrorTwice]: on_error call #1 (previous state: active), returning failure
[ERROR] [controller_manager.hardware_component.system.ErrorTwice]: on_error call #2 (previous state: finalized), returning failure
[ERROR] [controller_manager]: Deactivating following hardware components as their read cycle resulted in an error: [ ErrorTwice ]
```
Output, case 3 (`success`):
```
[WARN]  [controller_manager.hardware_component.system.ErrorTwice]: read() #10 returns ERROR (the only failure)
[ERROR] [controller_manager.hardware_component.system.ErrorTwice]: on_error call #1 (previous state: active), returning success
[ERROR] [controller_manager]: Deactivating following hardware components as their read cycle resulted in an error: [ ErrorTwice ]
```
Same result in every run: 3 runs per case (2 of them with an earlier version of this plugin that
differed only in names and formatting). I tested `FAILURE` only; `ERROR` takes the same `case` in `error()`.

<details><summary>src/error_twice_system.cpp</summary>

```cpp
// Reproduction for on_error() runs twice when it returns FAILURE.
#include <string>
#include "hardware_interface/system_interface.hpp"
#include "hardware_interface/types/hardware_interface_return_values.hpp"
#include "rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp"

namespace on_error_repro
{
class ErrorTwiceSystem : public hardware_interface::SystemInterface
{
public:
    CallbackReturn on_init(const hardware_interface::HardwareComponentInterfaceParams & params) override
    {
        if (SystemInterface::on_init(params) != CallbackReturn::SUCCESS){
            return CallbackReturn::ERROR;
        }

        const auto & p = get_hardware_info().hardware_parameters;

        if (p.count("on_error_result")){
            on_error_result_ = p.at("on_error_result");
        }
        else{
            on_error_result_ = "failure";
        }

        return CallbackReturn::SUCCESS;
    }

    hardware_interface::return_type read(const rclcpp::Time &, const rclcpp::Duration &) override
    {
        ++reads_;
        if (reads_ == 10){
            RCLCPP_WARN(get_logger(), "read() #%d returns ERROR (the only failure)", reads_);
            return hardware_interface::return_type::ERROR;
        }
        return hardware_interface::return_type::OK;
    }

    hardware_interface::return_type write(const rclcpp::Time &, const rclcpp::Duration &) override
    {
        return hardware_interface::return_type::OK;
    }

    CallbackReturn on_error(const rclcpp_lifecycle::State & previous_state) override
    {
        ++on_error_calls_;
        RCLCPP_ERROR(
            get_logger(), "on_error call #%d (previous state: %s), returning %s",
            on_error_calls_, previous_state.label().c_str(), on_error_result_.c_str());

        if (on_error_result_ == "success"){
            return CallbackReturn::SUCCESS;
        }
        else{
            return CallbackReturn::FAILURE;
```

**Expected behavior**

`on_error()` is called once per error, whatever it returns. A component that is already `FINALIZED`
should not get `on_error()` again.

**Environment**
 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64
 - Version: Jazzy, binary packages: ros-jazzy-hardware-interface 4.48.1, ros-jazzy-controller-manager 4.48.1
 - Code inspected on `master` @ 97e42adf87 as well: same logic.
 - No RT kernel (only the usual FIFO scheduling warning).

**Additional context**

No modifications to ros2_control.

Possible fixes, for discussion (I'm happy to open a PR with a test once the preferred approach is clear):
- (a) skip `on_error()` in `HardwareComponent::error()` also when the state is `FINALIZED`, or
- (b) call `error()` in only one place on the read/write error path (either `HardwareComponent::read()/write()`
  or `ResourceManager::read()/write()`).

(a) is the smaller change; (b) removes the duplication itself. Related: #1730 (added the second call),
#3620 (another consequence of the same error path: the "Error while attempting mode switch" log).
